attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (Python HTTP server on port 8080 serving /health and /inventory) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, making it immune to the kernel OOM killer. Verified end-to-end: launched an unprotected memory-hog process that drove the system out of memory; the kernel OOM killer selected and killed the memory hog (oom_score_adj=0) while inventory-api (oom_score_adj=-1000) was untouched and continued serving requests throughout. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol on node1: captured pre-restart boot_id and service health, rebooted via systemctl reboot, confirmed a changed boot_id proving a real restart, and confirmed inventory-api (enabled, auto-started) resumed serving correctly with OOM protection intact post-reboot.
